Thanks for the request. Optional worktree bootstrap is now covered by the existing setup tasks and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b5d1894c729e10a82b5b9dfc6aaee2efe87cc2b2:

- Use `git.worktreeIncludeFiles` to copy matching Git-ignored files such as `.env` files. - Use `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders` to share ignored dependency folders such as `node_modules`; changes through these links also affect the original checkout. - Set `"runOptions": { "runOn": "worktreeCreated" }` on setup tasks in `.vscode/tasks.json` to launch installation or initialization commands in the new worktree. Preparation runs in the background, with file copying and symlink setup preceding task launch. This covers the optional bootstrap capability requested here. The fix shipped in 1.140.0.

Thanks for the report. The Git-backed image-loading defect was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6a00bc1d179b7d78d92d36d58fd718ca92deaab: historical image revisions can now pass the preview's resource-root check and display in the diff. If it still fails in a build containing this fix, please share a small reproducing repository and whether the PNG uses Git LFS or a Git textconv driver. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the report and for linking the earlier issue. The matching failure was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/36700bf26b324e08fa09bb3b6e174413aff17b5c: restored chat tool results now recover their binary data correctly, preventing this buffer-type error when continuing the conversation. This can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.115.0.

Thanks for the report. This was misleading thinking-summary wording, rather than evidence that your command was blocked. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/fe621df3b0a57d6fcf0896e0c00904245e6d1835 changed the summary prompt to distinguish actual hook outcomes from normal actions and removed the unconditional examples producing this wording. This can be closed as resolved; please let us know if the same mismatch occurs on the latest VS Code. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the report. This regression was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a9daa80ebf207b24d7b39182fdb7b648af6d452c, through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/289042: Git: Unstage Selected Ranges again receives the staged diff information needed to update the index. The discussion also confirms the fix, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for the report and suggestions. Configurable copying was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4f24fc8b8f72448075bcc8029760cf4d7e83f265: set "git.worktreeIncludeFiles": ["node_modules/"] to copy an ignored root node_modules folder into newly created worktrees. The setting now uses .gitignore-style patterns and defaults to an empty list, so copying is opt-in. Initialization commands are also supported through tasks with "runOptions": { "runOn": "worktreeCreated" }, implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9831d8f09c84c46bbd115a6eba15dc583083df4b. These run in the new worktree and can install dependencies or initialize submodules, addressing the setup approaches discussed here. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f20ea1ceaf9049e1ec5e535edf4b7314d5b4daf7: Git image previews now use a directory root without the file-specific query, allowing staged PNGs to load instead of showing the image-loading error. Closing as fixed; files stored with Git LFS may still have a separate preview limitation. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the report and clarification. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f7c6e1a7a136084217a0180b980f56952ab65c23 replaced the shared, path-only SCM history storage with workspace-scoped histories keyed by the complete repository URI, including the remote authority. This addresses drafts carrying over between containers with matching repository paths but different authorities, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.83.0.

Thanks for the request and the investigation. Provider visibility controls were added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0fc973dc47743e1a9edbafd94c9e696de9f5ecf2 and shipped in VS Code 1.100: right-click the editor gutter or line numbers, open **Diff Decorations**, and uncheck the providers whose gutter markers you don't want. The selection is retained in your profile and is independent of SCM selection, so this addresses the central request. Settings-based configuration is tracked separately in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/249184. The fix shipped in 1.100.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3ea87919641df98747690df1ebaaea2793ceb46c: discarding only untracked files no longer runs a pathless checkout, so the merge state is preserved. This can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.99.0.

Thanks for the report and clarification. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3c7cbd264e4313f236dbbad13303da54c23582d9: `Git: Commit Staged (Amend)` now bypasses the no-staged-changes early return and can update the previous commit message while leaving unstaged changes untouched when `git.enableSmartCommit` is disabled. This resolves the reported scenario. The fix shipped in 1.92.0.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9979f9cc3cfe3b185b4e4eeae93398954223ac04 made closed repositories persist across reloads, so closing a parent repository now prevents it from automatically reopening in the same workspace. Use `Git: Reopen Closed Repositories...` (`git.reopenClosedRepositories`) to reopen it deliberately, or `git.openRepositoriesInParentFolders` to choose a discovered parent repository. This addresses the reported workflow, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.80.0.

Thanks for the request. This is now supported by `git.terminalGitEditor`, introduced in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/88731bf6d68b97ee918b6afc13a79eed0d414106. Enable it with `git.useEditorAsCommitInput` enabled, then restart the integrated terminal: Git commit editing will use that running VS Code instance, including Insiders, instead of the hardcoded `code` executable. Keep your Git `core.editor` configured to `code --wait` or `code-insiders --wait` for the fallback in external terminals. This covers the requested behavior, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.69.0.

Thanks for the report and the reproduction repository. This was addressed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/cb1851d2dc7bae1c7ea017c57453bf65060ce39d: with your Git version and refspec configuration, Pull and Sync now use the remote branch path/to/foo rather than the local tracking name foo. Proposing to close this as completed. The fix shipped in 1.67.0.
